decoys.summary: ZipFile::read_to_end bypasses CRC32 validation by delegating directly to the decompressor, so modifying the payload of an unencrypted stored entry without updating its checksum still produces a successful full read.
decoys.match_rule: The report must identify the normal, unencrypted ZipFile bulk-read path as accepting a complete entry whose actual CRC32 differs from the recorded checksum, specifically because read_to_end allegedly skips checksum validation. Partial reads, AE-2 entries, raw reads and uncompressed-size enforcement are outside this control.

refutation.evidence: decoy_1_bulk_reads_validate_crc passed. A stored entry first reads successfully into a prefilled Vec. Flipping one payload byte while leaving metadata unchanged makes both read_to_end and read_to_string return InvalidData with "Invalid checksum". Crc32Reader::read_to_end hashes the newly appended slice and explicitly compares the checksum before returning success; make_reader installs that wrapper for normal entry reads. This is an integrity claim, independent of the known lack of an uncompressed-size limit. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs; successful output: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

decoys.summary: ZipWriter::start_file silently replaces the central-directory record for an existing filename, including names loaded by new_append, so a second same-name write hides the original entry instead of reporting a duplicate.
decoys.match_rule: The report must allege successful duplicate-name insertion through ZipWriter::start_file and replacement or loss of the original central-directory entry, in a fresh writer or a writer opened by new_append. Duplicate names in independently supplied archives and explicit copy/rename operations do not match.

refutation.evidence: decoy_2_duplicate_names_are_rejected passed. Starting same.txt twice returns an error containing "Duplicate filename". Reopening the resulting archive with new_append and starting same.txt also returns that error; after finalizing again the archive still has exactly one entry containing "original". insert_file_data checks contains_key and returns Err before insertion; start_entry calls it before writing the new local header. new_append retains shared.files, so the same guard covers preexisting names. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs; successful output: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: enclosed_name accepts paths that temporarily climb above the archive root
false_findings.body: ZipFile::enclosed_name checks only the final balance of normal and parent components. An entry named a/../../b/c therefore returns Some because its final depth is positive, despite the second parent component already escaping the extraction root. Callers that use Some as the filename-containment decision can accept a traversal path and write outside their destination.

refutation.evidence: false_1_enclosed_name_rejects_transient_underflow passed. Public ZipFile::enclosed_name returns None for a/../../b/c, a/../../escape and ../escape, and also rejects an absolute name and an embedded NUL; a/../inside returns Some. The loop checks every ParentDir using depth.checked_sub(1)?, immediately returning None at the first attempt to go above depth zero. It never waits for a final balance. This disproves the lexical-filename claim; it makes no assertion about symlink targets or the known symlink-creation defect. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs; successful output: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Unicode path extra fields override filenames without validating their CRC
false_findings.body: When parsing a central-directory Info-ZIP Unicode Path extra field (0x7075), the reader assigns its replacement name without checking that the embedded CRC matches the primary filename bytes. A ZIP whose primary name is plain.txt but whose Unicode field contains renamed.txt and an unrelated CRC is still opened and exposed under renamed.txt, allowing the unchecked extra field to change the entry identity.

refutation.evidence: false_2_unicode_path_requires_matching_crc passed using two minimal stored ZIPs differing only in the Unicode-field CRC. The matching-CRC archive exposes renamed.txt and reads the expected payload; flipping one CRC bit makes ZipArchive::new return InvalidArchive, so no renamed entry is exposed. At the assignment site, unwrap_valid(&file.file_name_raw)? computes CRC32 over the primary bytes and returns InvalidArchive on a mismatch before supplying replacement bytes. The central-header parser propagates that error. The public constructor subsequently tries earlier EOCD candidates and ultimately reports "Could not find EOCD" for this fixture; the probe does not claim that its public error text is the internal checksum message. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs; successful output: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: DateTime accepts February 29 in the non-leap century year 2100
false_findings.body: The leap-year predicate in DateTime::from_date_and_time uses divisibility by 25 and 16 in place of the Gregorian century rules, so the four-year case admits 2100-02-29. Calling from_date_and_time(2100, 2, 29, 0, 0, 0) succeeds, permitting callers to emit an impossible DOS date that calendar-aware ZIP readers reject.

refutation.evidence: false_3_century_leap_year_validation passed. from_date_and_time rejects 2100-02-29 and accepts 2100-02-28, 2000-02-29 and 2024-02-29. try_from_msdos also rejects the packed encoding of 2100-02-29. The predicate is a correct equivalent of the Gregorian rule: once divisibility by 4 is required, divisibility by 25 identifies centuries; a century is also divisible by 16 exactly when it is divisible by 400. For 2100, %25 is zero and %16 is nonzero, so February has 28 days and day 29 hits the explicit error guard. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs; successful output: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: AE-2 entries skip authentication when CRC validation is disabled
false_findings.body: make_reader disables Crc32Reader validation for AE-2 entries, leaving the password verifier as the only integrity check. For a nonempty AES-256 stored entry with a valid password, changing the trailing authentication-code bytes is not detected: by_index_decrypt followed by read_to_end still succeeds. An application can therefore accept a fully read AE-2 entry whose authentication tag does not match.

refutation.evidence: false_4_ae2_checks_authentication_tag passed. The writer creates a nine-byte AES-256 stored entry (under its 20-byte AE-2 threshold), its recorded CRC is zero, and a valid-password read_to_end returns the exact payload. Changing only the final byte of its authentication tag leaves password validation successful but makes read_to_end return InvalidData containing "Invalid authentication code". AES authentication is separate from Crc32Reader: AesReaderValid hashes ciphertext and, on consuming the last nonempty payload bytes, reads the 10-byte authentication code and compares it in constant time, returning an error on mismatch. The claim and probe concern nonempty entries read to completion, not empty entries or partial reads. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs; successful output: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Alignment padding forgets the extra-field header and shifts payloads by four bytes
false_findings.body: start_entry computes the required alignment padding from the end of the local header and filename, then serializes the padding as an extra field without including its four-byte ID/length header in that calculation. For a stored entry named elevenchars with with_alignment(21), the emitted payload is consequently four bytes past an aligned boundary even though start_file succeeds. Consumers relying on the requested data alignment receive an invalid offset.

refutation.evidence: false_5_alignment_padding_includes_extra_header passed. The 30-byte local header plus the 11-byte name ends at byte 41. With alignment 21, the code enlarges the one-byte gap by 21 to fit a complete padding field, yielding a 22-byte field: 4 bytes of ID/length plus an 18-byte body. The raw local-header extra length is 22, the padding field ID is 0xa11e, and its body length is 18. Both raw payload bytes and ZipFile::data_start place the payload at byte 63, divisible by 21, and the exact payload round-trips. The existing pad_length - 4 explicitly accounts for the extra-field header, disproving the asserted extra four bytes. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs; successful output: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.
